City of Encinitas
City Council - 6:00 p.m.
AGENDA
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 26, 2017 -
6:00
p.m.
City of Encinitas - City Council Chambers
505 S. Vulcan Avenue
Encinitas, California 92024
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
2.

3.

4.

4A.
April is Fair Housing Month Proclamation
4B.

4C.
Presentation on the Climate Action Plan Update. Contact Person: CAP Program Administrator Najera
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a â€œWHITEâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. If at least two (2) Council Members agree, direction may be given to staff to put an item on a future agenda or provide additional information to answer a question.
6.
REPORT FROM CLOSED SESSION (IF HELD)
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a â€œPINKâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
8A.
Annual Progress Report on the implementation of the General Plan. Contact Person: Associate Planner Winter and Management Analyst Piano-Jones
Staff recommends that the Council approve the General Plan Annual Progress Report.
2017-04-26 Item 08A General Plan Annual Progress Report
8B.
Appointment to the Fire Governance Standing Subcommittee. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Mayor, with City Council approval, appoint Council Member Mosca as a representative on the Fire Governance Standing Subcommittee replacing Mayor Blakespear.
2017-04-26 Item 08B Fire Governance Appointment
8C.
Legislative Position Letter. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst McSeveney
Approve the legislative position letter for the Mayor's signature.
2017-04-26 Item 08C Legislative Position Letters
8D.
Facility Janitorial and Lockup Services Agreement. Contact Person: Park and Beach Superintendent Saul
City Council authorizes the City Manager to execute the Facility Janitorial and Lockup Services Agreement for City Parks, Beaches, and the Community/Senior Center with Blue Moon Management Corp. for the initial three-year term and authorize the City Manager to extend the contract for three (3) one-year renewal options upon satisfactory performance and mutual agreement for a total amount not to exceed $1,136,280.
2017-04-26 Item 08D Facility Janitorial and Lockup Services Agreement
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
10A.
Continued public hearing from March 22, 2017 to consider and approve Resolution No. 2017-28 approving the Fiscal Year (FY) 2017-18 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program budget and the FY 2017-18 Annual Action Plan. Contact Person: Management Analyst Piano-Jones
1) Adopt Resolution No. 2017-28 approving the proposed FY 2017-18 CDBG budget and FY 2017-18 Action Plan; 2) Authorize the City Manager to transmit the FY 2017-18 Action Plan and execute required certifications to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD); and 3) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute all funding agreements and documents consistent with the FY 2017-18 Action Plan.
2017-04-26 Item 10A Continued Public Hearing to Consider and Approve Resolution No. 2017-28 Approving FY 2017-18 Community Development Block Grant and Action Plan
10B.
Report back on the results of the one year Mediation Pilot Program and receive direction from Council on whether to continue the Mediation Program. Case Number: 15-174 POD. Contact Person: Principal Planner Langager
1) Consider the information in the Agenda Report; 2) Open the public hearing and receive and consider public testimony; 3) Approve Resolution No. 2017-36 titled, â€œA Resolution of the City of Encinitas City Council approving the continuation of a voluntary mediation program for general disputesâ€ (Attachment 1); and 4) Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with National Conflict Resolution Center for Mediation Services.
2017-04-26 Item 10B Report Back on Results of One Year Mediation Pilot Program
10C.
Status update for the Moonlight State Beach Marine Safety Center Project (CP14C). Contact Person: Associate Civil Engineer Kellar
It is recommended that City Council receive the update report.
2017-04-26 Item 10C Moonlight State Beach Marine Safety Center Project Status Update
10D.
Introduction of Municipal Tree Ordinance 2017-02 and Policy C027
Introduce the revised Municipal Tree Ordinance entitled "AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ENCINITAS, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 15.02 OF THE ENCINITAS MUNICIPAL CODE - MUNICIPAL TREE ORDINANCE"; adopt the revised Urban Forest Management Program Policy C027; and direct staff to begin soliciting applications for the Urban Forest Advisory Committee.
2017-04-26 Item 10D Municipal Tree Ordinance
10E.
Maintenance of the Coastal Rail Trail: Segment 39C
Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, in consultation with the City Attorney, to
sign a letter stating the City's intent to maintain the Coastal Rail Trail Segment 39C
within the South Coast Highway 101 right-of-way.
2017-04-26 Item 10E CRT Maintenance - Agenda Report
10F.Ad
option of Resolution 2017-34 approving an off-cycle budget appropriation of $279,944 to provide additional funding for the Coastal Mobility and Livability Study (CMLS) to augment the costs and the scope of work for the completion of the Rail Corridor Vision Study (RCVS) and for the preparation of a Quiet Zone Feasibility Study.
1. Adopt Resolution No. 2017-34 (Attachment 1) approving an off-cycle budget
appropriation of $279,944 to the Rail Corridor Vision Study (RCVS) component of the
CMLS (WC15A) project budget, with a total of $47,717 to be applied to the overall RCVS
work effort and $232,227 for a Quiet Zone Feasibility Study; and
2. Authorize the City Manager, in consultation with the City Attorney, to sign contract
amendment #2 (Attachment 2) with Parsons Brinckerhoff to augment the costs and the
scope of work for the completion of the RCVS and the preparation of a Quiet Zone
Feasibility Study
2017-04-26 Item 10F CMLS Budget Request

ADJOURNMENT
Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
